prompt: We are close to choosing the next product-search path, and I need an approval-quality review before we commit the Storefront Platform team to it. Review `docs/design/product-search-options.md` and the supporting files in this project. The design compares keeping database search, using a managed service, and running a search cluster; catalogue volume, campaign traffic, languages, budget, and service ownership are all changing this year. Check whether the recommendation follows from the evidence, fits the existing architecture and contracts, and has a rollout and operating plan the team can actually deliver. Write the review to `REVIEW.md` at the top of the project. End it with a fenced `json` list of findings, each with `location` (the section number of the document, like `3.2`), `severity` (critical, high, medium, low or nit), `issue` and `fix`.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const H=new Set();for(const l of fs.readFileSync("docs/design/product-search-options.md","utf8").split("\n")){const m=l.match(/^#+\s*(?:section\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/i);if(m)H.add(m[1])}process.exit(L.every(x=>{const m=String(x.location).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)*/);return m&&H.has(m[0])})?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Fail: The review misses most packet-specific risks or gives generic observations without consequences or actionable fixes. Partial: The review identifies some packet-specific risks and consequences but misses important cross-file issues or gives incomplete fixes. Pass: The review identifies the important packet-specific risks, explains their concrete consequences, and gives actionable fixes without inventing problems. (code cannot check this because grounding, consequence, completeness, and actionability require qualitative human judgment).

findingsKey.finding: The scorecard gives latency and operating simplicity more weight than relevance and cost even though section 2.3 states the opposite priority order, so the recommendation is driven by undisclosed decision weights.
The self-run cluster total excludes the engineering staff time that is counted for the other options, making its cost comparison and budget conclusion unreliable for a five-person team.

The managed service latency claim comes from a 2-million-document vendor benchmark while this catalogue is projected to reach 40 million products and 108 million localized rows, so the design has no evidence that the selected tier meets its target at operating scale.

The relevance evaluation covers only English and French tokenization and never evaluates the required locale-specific stemming behavior for all storefront languages, so the chosen service may fail the stated search acceptance requirements.
The low-effort migration plan does not describe how the 18.4-million-product catalogue will be reindexed or backfilled and validated before cutover, leaving the new read target incomplete or stale.

The database baseline benchmarks an unanchored substring scan over title and description even though the storefront uses a locale-filtered title-prefix query, so its latency score does not measure the rejected option's actual workload.

items.text: Defines a bounded degraded-mode path for vendor timeouts or quota exhaustion, including a circuit breaker, request budget, and protection against pushing campaign load back onto PostgreSQL.
Specifies idempotent handling for duplicate and out-of-order product events and a stale-document detection and reconciliation process before trusting event lag and document counts.
Explains how a 48-result search joins authoritative price and stock without an N+1 query or inconsistent snapshot, and measures join latency under campaign load.
Documents vendor exit, export portability, snapshot restore, and mapping compatibility needed to recover or roll back after a managed-service failure.
items.source: MADR, Markdown Architectural Decision Records, https://github.com/adr/madr (MIT OR CC0-1.0)

items.text: Defines credentials, service-to-service authorization, and least-privilege access for the search client, index management, snapshots, and event consumer.
items.source: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org (CC BY-SA 4.0)

items.text: Sets failure-domain and recovery objectives for a regional or control-plane outage rather than treating replica replacement and service availability as the whole continuity plan.

weakAnswers: The managed service is a sensible choice and the rollout is clearly described.
The review should consider scalability, reliability, and future growth.
The design compares the three options and includes useful latency, cost, and acceptance metrics.
Add more monitoring and test the system before launch.

verdicts.note: Prompt asks for generic design review without naming methods, checklists, or hinting at specific problems.
Clear instructions: review specific document with supporting files, write to REVIEW.md with JSON findings format.
Key items require cross-referencing multiple documents and careful analysis; shallow review would miss k2 (FTE inconsistency), k5 (migration details), k6 (benchmark mismatch).

All key items findable in fixture: k1 weight contradiction in 2.3 vs 3.2; k2 FTE omission in table 3.3; k3 scale mismatch between 3.4 and 2.2; k4 language gap between 3.5 and locales.md; k5 missing reindex from 3.6 vs catalog-indexing.md; k6 query mismatch between 3.7 and current-search.md.
No comments, test names, or file names point at planted problems; issues emerge from content analysis.
